ayahOccurrences.text: لَن يَضُرُّوكُمْ إِلَّآ أَذًى ۖ وَإِن يُقَٰتِلُوكُمْ يُوَلُّوكُمُ ٱلْأَدْبَارَ ثُمَّ لَا يُنصَرُونَ

ayahOccurrences.text: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ آمِنُوا بِمَا نَزَّلْنَا مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا مَعَكُم مِّن قَبْلِ أَن نَّطْمِسَ وُجُوهًا فَنَرُدَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَدْبَارِهَآ أَوْ نَلْعَنَهُمْ كَمَا لَعَنَّآ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلسَّبْتِ ۚ وَكَانَ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفْعُولًا

ayahOccurrences.text: وَمَن يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهُۥٓ إِلَّا مُتَحَرِّفًا لِّقِتَالٍ أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزًا إِلَىٰ فِئَةٍ فَقَدْ بَآءَ بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَأْوَىٰهُ جَهَنَّمُ ۖ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ

ayahOccurrences.text: قُلْ مَن يَرْزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ أَمَّن يَمْلِكُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَمَن يُخْرِجُ ٱلْحَىَّ مِنَ ٱلْمَيِّتِ وَيُخْرِجُ ٱلْمَيِّتَ مِنَ ٱلْحَىِّ وَمَن يُدَبِّرُ ٱلْأَمْرَ ۚ فَسَيَقُولُونَ ٱللَّهُ ۚ فَقُلْ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ

lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: ٱلْأَدْبَارَ is in the derivative form: دُبُرٌ
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
د/ب/ر   d–b–r back, backside, buttocks, the tail end, to turn one’s back
; to boycott; to plan, to arrange, to organise, to prepare; to depart, to die; root, origin.

Of this root, 11 forms occur 44 times in the Qur’an:
يُدَبِّرُ yudabbir 4 times; يَتَدَبَّرُ yatadabbar 2 times; يَدَّبَّرُ yaddabbar 2 times; أَدْبَرَ ʾadbara 4 times; مُدَبِّرَاتٌ mudabbirāt 1 time; مُدْبِرٌ mudbir 2 times; مُدْبِرُون mudbirūn 6 times; إِدْبَارٌ ʾidbār 1 time; دَابِرٌ dābir 4 times; دُبُرٌ dubur 5 times and أَدْبَارٌ ʾadbār 13 times.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
دُبُرٌ dubur I [n., pl. ʾadbār] back, backside, end part, the last part

(12:27) وَإِنْ كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِنْ دُبُرٍ فَكَذَبَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ but if his shirt has been torn from the back, then she has lied and he is one of the truthful; *

(33:15) يُوَلُّونَ الأَدْبَارَ they turn tail; *

(15:65) اتَّبِعْ أَدْبَارَهُمْ walk behind them [lit. follow their backs]; *

(4:47) نَطْمِسَ وُجُوهًا فَنَرُدَّهَا عَلَى أَدْبَارِهَا We deprive a [few] people of [Our] direction, turning them on their heels, or, We shame them and frustrate their hopes [lit. We obliterate faces and turn them upon their backs] II [adverbially] at the end, closely after

(50:40) وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَارَ السُّجُودِ proclaim His praise in the night and at the end of every prayer [lit. prostration].

entries.definitionHtml:

(15:65) اتَّبِعْ أَدْبَارَهُمْ walk behind them [lit. follow their backs]; *

(4:47) نَطْمِسَ وُجُوهًا فَنَرُدَّهَا عَلَى أَدْبَارِهَا We deprive a [few] people of [Our] direction, turning them on their heels, or, We shame them and frustrate their hopes [lit. We obliterate faces and turn them upon their backs] II [adverbially] at the end, closely after

entries.label: دَابِرٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
دَابِرٌ dābir [n.] origin, root, the last part, the end part

(7:72) وَقَطَعْنَا دَابِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا We cut the roots of those who denied Our revelations.

entries.label: إِدْبَارٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
إِدْبَارٌ ʾidbār [v. n.] (act of) retreating, setting, fading [of stars]

(52:49) وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَإِدْبَارَ النُّجُوم ِ glorify Him at night and at the fading of the stars.

entries.label: أَدْبَرَ
entries.definitionHtml:
أَدْبَرَ ʾadbara [v. IV, intrans.]

1 to turn one’s back on, to turn down

(70:17) تَدْعُوا مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّى it will call [claim] the one who turns his back [on the truth] and runs away

2 to retreat, to recede

(74:33) وَاللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ by the night when it recedes!

entries.label: مُدبِرٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
مُدبِرٌ mudbir [act. part., pl. مُدْبِرُون mudbirūn] turning one’s back, turning away, running away, taking to one’s heels

(27:10) وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَآهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَانٌّ وَلَّى مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ ‘And throw down your staff,’ but when he saw it writhing like a snake (or, a demon), he turned tail and fled, and did not come back.

entries.label: مُدَبِّرَاتٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
مُدَبِّرَاتٌ mudabbirāt [pl. of fem. act. part. مُدَبِّرَةٌ mudabbiratun] those planning, carrying out, managing, executing

(79:5) فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْرًا and those bringing the matter to an end!

entries.label: يَتَدَبَّرُ
entries.definitionHtml:
يَتَدَبَّرُ yatadabbar [imperf. of v. V تَدَبَّرَ tadabbara, trans.] to contemplate, to ponder upon, to meditate on

(47:24) أَفَلاَ يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْءَانَ أَمْ عَلَى قُلُوبٍ أَقْفَالُهَا do they not contemplate the Qur’an?, or is it that hearts [still] have their own locks placed upon them?

entries.label: يَدَّبَّرُ
entries.definitionHtml:
يَدَّبَّرُ yaddabbar [imperf. of v. VIII ادَّبَّرَ ʾiddabbara, an assimilated form of v. اتْدَبَّرَ ʾitdabbara, trans.] to contemplate, to ponder upon, to examine carefully

(23:68) أَفَلَمْ يَدَّبَّرُوا الْقَوْلَ أَمْ جَاءَهُمْ مَا لَمْ يَأْتِ ءَابَاءَهُمُ الأَوَّلِينَ have they not contemplated the Word [of God]?, or has there come to them something that did not come to their forefathers?

entries.label: يُدَبِّرُ
entries.definitionHtml:
يُدَبِّرُ yudabbir [imperf. of v. II دَبَّرَ dabbara, trans.] to manage, to govern, to execute

(10:31) ... وَمَنْ يُدَبِّرُ الأَمْرَ فَسَيَقُولُونَ اللَّهُ ‘… and who governs everything?’, they are sure to say, ‘God.’
